newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says Asian trade ties to expand after EU dispute.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Asian trade ties to expand after EU dispute.

text.p: Iran has told members of the Association of South East Asian Nations that it would boost trade ties with Asia after a dispute with the European Union, the Iranian news agency IRNA said Thursday.

"'Look east' policies will be brighter in the future and Iran's ties with Asian countries will be expanded with greater momentum," Iranian deputy foreign minister Alaeddin Boroujerdi told ASEAN envoys to Tehran in remarks reported by the agency.

"Europe will be the main loser in this game," he said in reference to the dispute over a German court verdict that accused Tehran leaders of ordering the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin. Iran has denied involvement.

"The recent developments proved this principle more than ever before that the Asian countries...should strengthen ties and expand links with each other even more," Boroujerdi told the ambassadors of Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines and Brunei. ASEAN also groups Singapore and Vietnam.
